slides.title: Chasing isn't hard. **Rewriting it** every time is.
paras: Where the time really goes: checking who's late, staring at a blank email, worrying about tone, then putting it off another week.
Fix the writing once and the rest becomes a calendar reminder.

steps.d: Assume it slipped. Resend the invoice.
Restate the amount and how to pay.
Give a new date and the next step.

steps.t: Still nothing: pick up the phone
steps.d: Then do what your terms say: pause work or add the agreed fee.

cards.title: Payment reminders
cards.text: Write 3 payment reminder emails for [BUSINESS]. Email 1 (1 day late): friendly, assume it slipped. Email 2 (7 days): clear, restate the amount and how to pay. Email 3 (14 days): firm but polite, give a new date and the next step: [NEXT STEP]. Under 80 words each. Use placeholders for client, invoice, amount and dates.

slides.note: Keep the placeholders. Fill in client details in your email app.

messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT NAME],
Just a quick note: invoice [INVOICE NO.] for [AMOUNT] was due on [DATE]. It may have slipped through, so I've attached it again.
If it's already on its way, thank you, and please ignore this.
Best, [YOUR NAME]

slides.note: Example: a freelance web designer, invented.

before.label: THE EMAIL I KEPT PUTTING OFF
before.text: Hi, so sorry to bother you, just wondering if you maybe had a chance to look at the invoice? No worries if not!

after.label: AI DRAFT
after.text: Hi [CLIENT NAME], I'm following up on invoice [INVOICE NO.] for [AMOUNT], now 7 days overdue. Could you let me know when to expect payment? You can pay by [PAYMENT METHOD], and I'm happy to resend anything you need.

slides.note: Clear isn't rude. It names the invoice, the amount and the ask.

messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT NAME],
Invoice [INVOICE NO.] for [AMOUNT] is now 14 days overdue, and I haven't heard back.
Please arrange payment by [NEW DATE]. If it isn't received by then, I'll [NEXT STEP] as set out in our terms.
If something's wrong, just reply and let's sort it out.
[YOUR NAME]

slides.note: Only charge late fees your contract allows.

caption:
How to chase late payments politely: a 3-step reminder email system

Chasing an invoice takes a few minutes. Rewriting the same awkward email every time is what eats the afternoon.

Copy this once:

"Write 3 payment reminder emails for [BUSINESS]. Email 1 (1 day late): friendly, assume it slipped. Email 2 (7 days): clear, restate the amount and how to pay. Email 3 (14 days): firm but polite, give a new date and the next step: [NEXT STEP]. Under 80 words each. Use placeholders for client, invoice, amount and dates."

Then:
1) Save the 3 drafts as templates.
2) Add calendar reminders for day 1, 7 and 14.
3) Fill in client details in your email app, not in the chat.

Only charge late fees your contract allows.
